div.head: Wi 7
div.ab: Gif bescoren man steorleas gange him an gestliðnesse, gefe him man ænes; ⁊ þæt ne geweorðe buton he leafnesse habbe, þæt hine man læng feormige.
Gif bescoren man steorleas gange him an gestliðnesse, gefe him man ænes; ⁊ þæt ne geweorðe, buton he leafnesse habbe, þæt hine man læng feormige.
Gif bescoren man steorleas gange him an gestliðnesse, gefe him man ænes, ⁊ þæt ne geweorðe, buton he leafnesse habbe, þæt hine man læng feormige.

Wenn ein [als Geistlicher] beschorener Mann regelwidrig für sich schweift auf Gastfreundschaft, gebe man [sie] ihm [nur] einmal; und das geschehe nicht (ausser wenn er Urlaub hat), dass man ihn länger beherberge.
If a tonsured man [as a cleric] wanders irregularly on his own in search of hospitality, let [it] be given him [only] once; and let it not happen (unless he has leave) that he is lodged longer.

If a tonsured man, [who is] not under ecclesiastical discipline, wanders about looking for hospitality, once [only] shall it be granted to him, and unless he has permission, he shall not be entertained further.
If a tonsured man, who is under no [ecclesiastical] authority seeks hospitality, he is to be given it once; and it is not to happen that he is harboured longer, unless he has permission.

If a tonsured man not under [any ecclesiastical/monastic] rule seeks out hospitality for himself, one should give it to him once; and it should not happen that he be supported for a longer time, unless he should have permission.

note.seg: ‘not living under the rule of any religious house’ Toller, zu eng; richtiger ‘unkanonisch, in neglect of rule’ (Stubbs Councils III 234), denn steor heisst disciplina. Die Quelle für Wi s. Gl Fremde 2a. Es ist nicht bloss Stiftsklerus gemeint. Bei Mönchen verbot die Synode a. 673 c. 4 einfach das Wechseln des Klosters. Bescoren (Toller Suppl. s. v.) preost übersetzt im 9. Jh. attonsus clericus. Flüchtige Mönche oder Kleriker aufzunehmen, besonders in Klöster der Laienäbte, war ein Missbrauch, gegen den Beda Ad Egbertum 12 und dieser Egbert Dial. 7 eifern. Als Gewährer der Gastfreundschaft denke man nicht bloss Laien, sondern namentlich geistliche Stifter, wo allein man des Bischofs systaticae (s. Ducange) lesen konnte

‘not living under the rule of any religious house’ Toller, too narrow; more correctly ‘uncanonically, in neglect of rule’ (Stubbs Councils III 234), for steor means disciplina. For the source of Wi see Gl Fremde 2a. Not only the clergy of collegiate foundations are meant. In the case of monks, the synod a. 673 c. 4 simply forbade changing from one monastery to another. Bescoren (Toller Suppl. s. v.) preost translates attonsus clericus in the 9th cent. Receiving fugitive monks or clerics, especially in monasteries of lay abbots, was an abuse against which Beda Ad Egbertum 12 and this same Egbert Dial. 7 inveigh. As grantors of hospitality one should think not only of laymen but especially of ecclesiastical foundations, where alone the bishop’s systaticae (see Ducange) could be read
Dativus ethicus; see that word in Wb 46
Über gestliðnesse vgl. Klaeber in Anglia 21, 282
On gestliðnesse cf. Klaeber in Anglia 21, 282
For the meaning of steorleas Liebermann refers to Stubbs, Councils, iii. 234.

note.label: authority
note.seg: Like clauses 4–6 of the canons of Hertford of 672, this law is directed against clergy who wander from diocese to diocese. It is probably not meant to apply only to monks outside their cloister.

note.label: man
note.seg: That is, a man with his head shaved in the tonsure of a cleric.
